files.README.md:
# Harbor Shop

A small storefront, its orders API, and the inventory service behind them.

- `apps/storefront` is the web shop.
- `apps/api` serves orders.
- `docs` explains how to run it.

# Getting started

content.text: The featured shelf reads a static catalog through `featured()`. I'll add an optional `special` to `Product`, a `weeklySpecial(today)` lookup next to `featured()`, and a `WeeklySpecial` card at the head of the shelf. The existing test pins the featured order, so I'll add a test for the special rather than change it.

rawOutput.output:
> harbor-shop@1.4.0 test
> vitest run

 ✓ src/api/products.test.ts > lists the featured products
 ✗ src/api/products.test.ts > offers the weekly special until it ends
   AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'rope'
   - Expected: "rope"
   + Received: undefined

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)

content.text: The failure is the test setup, not the lookup: `catalog.setup.ts` strips every unfeatured product before each test, so the rope coaster never reaches `weeklySpecial`. I'll keep products on special in that filter.

content.oldText:
// Tests run against featured items only.
beforeEach(() => catalog.splice(0, catalog.length, ...catalog.filter(product => product.featured)));
content.newText:
// Tests run against featured items and anything on special.
beforeEach(() => catalog.splice(0, catalog.length, ...catalog.filter(product => product.featured || product.special)));

productDecisions.headline: Crop a long task title rather than wrapping it
productDecisions.detail: Queue rows keep one line each. A title that does not fit is cut with an ellipsis, so every row is the same height and the queue can be read as an order rather than as a list of paragraphs.
productDecisions.evidence: Three of the eight open issues have titles over 60 characters. Wrapped, they made rows twice the height of the others and the order stopped being obvious at a glance.

productDecisions.headline: Put the reorder grip on the left of each queued row
productDecisions.detail: The drag handle sits left of the title, where a thumb reaches it without covering the text being moved. The destructive action stays on the right.
productDecisions.evidence: Matches the iOS calendar, which the product owner pointed at. Keeping dequeue on the right means a mis-grab moves a task rather than removing one.
productDecisions.note: Yes — never put destructive and drag on the same side.

productDecisions.headline: Queue the work on the Server rather than on the host
productDecisions.detail: An issue being open on GitHub does not put it in front of an agent. Somebody picks it into a queue the Server owns, and the agents draw from that in order.
productDecisions.evidence: The host cannot assign work to an agent, and assignment there meant anything opened overnight was picked up unreviewed.

productDecisions.headline: Ship the importer before the exporter
productDecisions.detail: Importing a catalogue from a spreadsheet lands first. Export waits for the next release.
productDecisions.evidence: Every trial shop so far arrived with a spreadsheet and nothing to export yet. Nobody has asked to take data out.

productDecisions.headline: Keep the cart total on the server, not in the client
productDecisions.detail: Totals, discounts and tax are computed server-side and the client only renders them. The cart posts line items and reads back a priced cart.
productDecisions.evidence: Two promo bugs came from the client and server disagreeing on rounding. One source of truth removes the class of bug rather than the instances.

productDecisions.headline: Let each surface own its own data reads
productDecisions.detail: A screen asks for what it shows instead of a shared store holding everything. Two screens wanting the same thing ask twice.
productDecisions.evidence: The shared store had become the reason unrelated screens re-rendered, and it was the first thing anyone had to understand to change anything.
productDecisions.note: Too far. Shared reads are fine; it was the global store that hurt.
